Reversibility is exact: 11,146 collisions were run forward and then inverted, recovering every bit of the initial state. Nothing in the dynamics is stochastic. Kulik September 2026 Lead-in Put some indistinguishable tokens on the vertices of a finite graph, one per vertex, and let a token step to an empty neighbour. That is the whole system. The graph is the substrate; the space of configurations and legal steps is the arena. Now change something about it — add an edge, subdivide one, glue two vertices together, allow a site to hold two tokens instead of one, or simply look at the system with a coarser symmetry. Each of those changes alters which transformations exist. The question this paper asks is narrow and answerable: When the rules of movement change, what happens to the structure that was there before? The naive answers are that structure is created or destroyed. Both turn out to be wrong in a precise and checkable sense. Every elementary change either extends the transformation structure, re-expresses it, or hides it from a particular observer. Structure is never annihilated. The one operation that does produce a genuine kernel — restricting which configurations are admissible — produces it as a relative cohomology class: something present in the larger admissible space and absent from the smaller one, with an exact dimension formula. The headline object is a single integer attached to each such restriction. For a distinguished site allowed to hold 𝑟 tokens instead of 𝑟 + 1, that integer is the first Betti number of a small quotient graph, and it can be computed without ever building the arena. Kulik September 2026 What this is, and what changed This is not a theorem paper. It proves nothing and is separable from every result it draws on. Its purpose is the move the programme has always required: state the thing forward, run it backward, and look at where the two readings cancel. The first version of this piece concluded that a reader has two coordinates — resolution, which decides what can be told apart, and relation, which decides what counts as having happened twice. That was too weak, and the correction is the substance of this version. There are not two coordinates. There is one operation — declare some differences inessential, keep what survives — applied at successive orders of structure. Resolution is that operation acting on states and transitions. Relation is the same operation acting on routes. What looked like a second axis is the next application of the first. That correction is not adopted on its merits as prose. Section 5 reports that computation. It does recur, and the remainders disagree case by case — which is the strongest available evidence that this is a tower and not a metaphor for two things. Kulik September 2026 Abstract An n-bit modular adder is read two ways, and both readings are computed exactly. Theorem A (the reader cut). Present the input positions of (a,b) ↦ a+b mod 2ⁿ in an arbitrary order. The minimal Myhill–Nerode state count after a set S of positions has been read depends only on S — never on the order used to reach it — and factorises over the maximal runs of S: F(S) = PROD over maximal runs [l,r] of S of f(l,r) f(l,r) = 1 if [l,r] = [0,n-1] L = r - l + 1 2 if l = 0 and r < n-1 L+1 if l > 0 and r = n-1 2L+1 if 0 < l <= r < n-1 Memory is a cut functional, not a history functional. Theorem B (the relation residual). Model the same machine as a Cayley complex on ℤ/2ⁿ with generators 2⁰,…,2ⁿ⁻¹, declaring a square whenever its two moves touch disjoint bits. Then b_1^disjoint(n) = C(n,2) + (n-1) = (n-1)(n+2)/2 Both hold for all n. They are different invariants — one a rank, additive over pairs and identical for every reader; the other a state count, multiplicative over the runs of a cut and different for every reading order — and a once-plausible conjecture equating them is refuted structurally rather than numerically. What the two share is a sufficient statistic. On the object side the class of an undeclared square keeps only a seam bit and a carry-run depth; on the reader side a run keeps only a first-nontransparent depth and a carry mode. The exponentially large coordinate label — 2ⁿ basepoints there, 4^|S| assignments here — is in both cases the reader's own coordinates and not the object's structure. A change of base is then read as a whole divided down: the digits are the residues of repeated division and the carry is the quotient in transit. 23. Address on Eurythmy
From February 19 to March 3, 1921, Rudolf Steiner went on a lecture tour through the Netherlands, which included public eurythmy performances. The performances took place in Hilversum (February 20), Amsterdam (March 22 and 3), Rotterdam (26) and The Hague (February 27, 1921). Only Rudolf Steiner's eurythmy speeches in Hilversum and The Hague were recorded; in Amsterdam on March 3, Jan Stuten gave the introduction. A program with the German texts was created for the performances.
